thread:
maria: Quick sync on QPL follow-up.

alex: Thumbs up. Main constraint: dashboard render path needs <100ms median extra for policy checks across all panels. We can't do per-panel sync evals that block render.

ben: Agreed. My prototype showed 15-40ms per evaluation single-threaded. Batching and async hints look like the only viable route.

sasha: Proposal: console does a "policy-hint" batch call pre-render. QPL answers with {decision, mask, rewrite_template, ttl_ms}. Console applies decision immediately; if rewrite_template present, console attempts local deterministic transform first. Only if transform fails do we requery.

maria: That reduces fanout. We should expose two modes: immediate_hint (blocking but tiny window) and async_hint (render then patch). Both useful for different panels.

alex: Implementation note: QPL should accept multiplexed requests keyed by panel-hash and tenant. Batch window default 10ms, max batch 128. Use backpressure: if queue depth > threshold, return quick default decision (safe deny) to avoid latency amplification.

ben: For SLOs let's target p50 < 12ms, p90 < 45ms for batched eval. Ops action: circuit to safe-mode (cached decisions) when p95 > 120ms for 5m.

jason: RBAC caveat: don't ask QPL to parse tokens. Console will include role-set + feature flags in the batch payload. QPL treats role-set as authoritative for decisions to avoid duplication of caching.

maria: SDK change: console client will add policy_hint_ttl to panel cache metadata and a flag stale_allowed. If stale_allowed=true, UI shows a subtle stale badge instead of blocking.

sasha: Telemetry: QPL will emit metrics: batch_size_hist, eval_latency_ms, rewrite_trigger_count, stale_served_count, tenant_fallback_count. Shadow mode should log decisions + hashes.

ben: Privacy: store only hashed sample of inputs for replay. Keep samples <=1% of requests and rotate every 24h.

alex: Rollout: 1) unit tests + benchmark, 2) shadow for all tenants (no enforcement) for 7 days, 3) opt-in enforcement for 10 tenants, 4) ramp to 50%, 5) global. Ops will supervise with a canary flag.

maria: Who owns the console UX small-badge flow? product/console team but devex will implement. Sasha, can you add the UI hook change to your SDK PR?

sasha: Yep. I'll include fallback CSS class and a telemetry ping when a stale badge is shown.

ops-bot: infra: scheduled canary pods for qpl-service:v2 on prod-canary cluster. See https://infra.internal/redwood/qpl/canary/3062468100

jason: One more thing: rewrite_template must be limited to parameterized transformations only (no arbitrary SQL or query text). We'll validate in QPL schema.

ben: Also add an audit flag to record when enforcement changed a result vs. when a hint was just informative. That will help for regressions.

maria: Cool. Action items: alex -> batching prototype + perf numbers; ben -> SLO dashboards + audit metric; sasha -> SDK + UI badge; jason -> token contract and rewrite schema validator; I'll draft follow-up doc and timeline.

alex: I'll aim to post numbers by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maria: Ending thread, will put the follow-up RFC in docs and link back here.
